## Unreleased

### Security

- Label the plugin's token file with a no-read-up integrity level, so a lower-integrity process cannot read the token of an elevated x64dbg
- Disable `/api/load` unless `obsidian.ini` sets `[api] allow_load_binary=1`
- Validate `SET_REGISTER` values and `bpx` symbols in the plugin, and refuse `;` or control characters in every handler-built x64dbg command
- Cap plugin responses at the 1 MiB pipe frame; the server now reads exact lengths with timeouts and resets the pipe on a framing error instead of exiting
- Stop the bridge sending the bearer token through `HTTP_PROXY`/`HTTPS_PROXY`, and refuse redirects
- Bind the listener with `SO_EXCLUSIVEADDRUSE` instead of `SO_REUSEADDR`
- Make no network requests while checking a client certificate, and use the intermediates the client sends
- Throttle repeatedly failing remote peers and shorten the header and TLS handshake deadlines; bound pattern scans
- Use a per-session random pipe name created with `FILE_FLAG_FIRST_PIPE_INSTANCE`; the server verifies the pipe server's PID and connects at identification level
- Never write a pinned token to `%TEMP%`; pass the token to the server in a private environment block
- Open plugin output files by handle and verify their final location before writing
- Parse plugin requests as strict JSON and refuse duplicate keys; forward exactly `Content-Length` bytes
- Escape debuggee strings in coverage exports, decode `WRITE_MEMORY` hex strictly, reply to empty pipe frames, and terminate the server reliably on unload
- Require an exact `Origin` match, check the negotiated TLS protocol, and validate the server's token
- Build both binaries with `/guard:cf`, and `/CETCOMPAT` on x64
- Stop logging request bodies, cap the server text log, and keep pre-auth noise from filling the activity log

## v1.3.0 - 2026-11-22

### Changes

- Add threat-intel integrations: abuse.ch, MITRE ATT&CK, shared transport ([#11](https://github.com/Sarks0/binary-mcp/pull/11))
- Cut the tokens the server costs a model per session and per call ([#32](https://github.com/Sarks0/binary-mcp/pull/32))
- Fix confinement refusal disclosure and distinguish hard-link errors ([#17](https://github.com/Sarks0/binary-mcp/pull/17))
- fix: surface confinement denials instead of a reference ID ([#33](https://github.com/Sarks0/binary-mcp/pull/33))
- Add remote access support: HTTP transport with TLS and policy enforcement ([#18](https://github.com/Sarks0/binary-mcp/pull/18))
- ci: add Dependabot for uv.lock and the workflow action pins ([#16](https://github.com/Sarks0/binary-mcp/pull/16))
- Gate symbol-server PDB fetches on the binary's vendor, and fix 15 review findings ([#14](https://github.com/Sarks0/binary-mcp/pull/14))
- Gate releases on tests and derive the release notes from the commits ([#12](https://github.com/Sarks0/binary-mcp/pull/12))
- docs: cut the README to an overview and move detail into docs/ ([#15](https://github.com/Sarks0/binary-mcp/pull/15))
- Address integrator feedback: tool catalog, decompiler caveats, coverage locking, auto PDB, table-base xrefs ([#13](https://github.com/Sarks0/binary-mcp/pull/13))
- Dependency updates from Dependabot: [#19](https://github.com/Sarks0/binary-mcp/pull/19), [#20](https://github.com/Sarks0/binary-mcp/pull/20), [#21](https://github.com/Sarks0/binary-mcp/pull/21), [#22](https://github.com/Sarks0/binary-mcp/pull/22), [#23](https://github.com/Sarks0/binary-mcp/pull/23), [#24](https://github.com/Sarks0/binary-mcp/pull/24), [#25](https://github.com/Sarks0/binary-mcp/pull/25), [#28](https://github.com/Sarks0/binary-mcp/pull/28), [#29](https://github.com/Sarks0/binary-mcp/pull/29), [#30](https://github.com/Sarks0/binary-mcp/pull/30)
